facts.fact: Cyprian Keyes built his house on the site in 1734; he was a deacon of the Shrewsbury North Parish (later Boylston) church and a selectman when Boylston was incorporated in 1743. The house was later the Keyes-Dakin House, then Barlin Acres (NRHP 1982).
Cyprian Keyes was a founding member of the Town of Boylston and served as Selectman, Assessor and Town Clerk; flooring from the 1734 house was reclaimed for the clubhouse foyer.
The golf club (opened 11 August 1997, Mark Mungeam) stands on the estate; the clubhouse is on the site of the house.

concepts.name: The Deacon's Key
concepts.rationale: An old hand-forged brass key with a golf ball set in its bow: the Keyes name, and the 1734 homestead the course is built around.
concepts.symbolism: The key is a pun on the family name and a colonial door key of the kind an 18th-century house would have.
concepts.interpretation: The key's form is invented; no Keyes artefact is depicted.
concepts.strengths: One subject on the diagonal, readable at 32 px; the name in a picture without letters.
concepts.tradeoffs: A key is a general symbol; it says Keyes, not Boylston.

recommendation: Concept 1 (course chat 2026-10-31, under the developer's permission for overnight logos).
